narration: Here's a number that'll ruin your morning. Waiting ten years to start investing doesn't cost you a decade of returns — it costs you $418,000.
visual: Dark background. Giant '$418K' springs in from center in white. Two calendar icons labeled 'AGE 25' in green and 'AGE 35' in red appear below, each showing their final balance.

narration: Sarah starts at twenty-five — three hundred dollars a month. Forty years later, after investing $144,000 total, her account hits $798,000.
visual: Light background. Green piggy bank SVG springs in. A bar chart rises showing $798K final balance. '$144K invested' counter ticks up below the pig.

narration: Mike starts the exact same three hundred dollars a month — but at thirty-five. Same discipline, same returns. He only ends up with $380,000 at retirement.
visual: Dark background. Red piggy bank SVG (same design). A shorter bar rises to $380K. The gap between his result and Sarah's is impossible to ignore.

narration: Same money, same seven percent return, but ten years apart — the gap is $418,000. That's the real price of saying 'I'll start next year.'
visual: Light background. Two bars side by side — green $798K tall, red $380K noticeably shorter. A red badge springs in reading '$418K DIFFERENCE'.

narration: The wild part — that $418,000 gap isn't the missed contributions. It's compound interest on the compound interest. Ten extra years of compounding snowballs into everything.
visual: Dark background. Exponential growth curve animates across a chart from age 25 to 65. A dashed red line marks 'Start at 35' showing the portion of the curve that's missed.

narration: The best time to start was yesterday. The second-best time is right now. Even fifty dollars a month today beats waiting for the perfect moment.
visual: Light background. Calendar SVG with today's date circled in amber. A 'START NOW' button springs in. '$50/month beats waiting' text fades in below.
